data.title: VanEck to end Gemini ETF custody deals, keeps Coinbase
data.description:
VanEck is cutting ties with Gemini as a custodian across three cryptocurrency exchange-traded funds (ETFs), ending a relationship that began with its first spot Bitcoin ETF.

VanEck notified Gemini on Monday that it would terminate custody and clearing agreements for its Bitcoin (BTC), Ether (ETH) and Solana (SOL) ETFs, according to separate filings with the US Securities and Exchange Commission (SEC) on Thursday.

The agreements will end “on or about” Feb. 16, 2027, while Coinbase Custody, which already serves the funds, will continue providing custody services.

The move raises questions about Gemini’s position in the US spot crypto ETF market, where Coinbase serves as custodian for many of the largest funds. The filings did not disclose the reasons for the terminations.

VanEck to also end Gemini’s Solana staking arrangement

The termination extends beyond cryptocurrency custody. VanEck’s Solana ETF (VSOL) filing also covers a Gemini staking services agreement, raising questions about how the fund will handle staking after the transition.

Staking allows tokenholders to earn rewards by helping secure a proof-of-stake (PoS) blockchain such as Solana. For ETFs that stake their holdings, the service can provide an additional source of returns for the fund.

Cointelegraph contacted VanEck and Gemini for comment on the reason for terminating the agreements and the potential impact on the Solana ETF’s staking operations, but had not received a response by publication.

Winklevoss brothers helped pioneer spot Bitcoin ETFs

Gemini’s founders, Cameron and Tyler Winklevoss, were among the earliest proponents of spot Bitcoin ETFs in the United States, filing to launch the Winklevoss Bitcoin Trust in July 2013. US regulators did not approve the first spot Bitcoin ETFs until January 2024, more than a decade after the brothers’ initial filing.

Gemini became the original Bitcoin custodian for VanEck’s spot Bitcoin ETF when the fund launched in January 2024, before VanEck added Coinbase Custody in June that year.

VanEck’s Bitcoin ETF (HODL) is considerably smaller than the largest US spot Bitcoin funds, holding about $880 million in assets under management, compared with $47.6 billion for BlackRock’s iShares Bitcoin Trust (IBIT) and $10.6 billion for Fidelity’s Wise Origin Bitcoin Fund (FBTC), according to Wallet Pilot data as of Thursday.

Gemini has also provided custody services for crypto ETFs in Canada and Australia. In the US, it continues to serve as a custodian for at least one smaller fund, the 7RCC Spot Bitcoin and Carbon Credit Futures ETF (BTCK), which identified Gemini and BitGo as its Bitcoin custodians in a September 2026 regulatory filing.

data.title: Asia report: Nikkei and KOSPI drop 5% as AI sell-off intensifies
data.description:
Asian markets were following in the footsteps of a sell-off on Wall Street overnight despite a blockbuster IPO from Claude maker Anthropic, as investors pulled money away from stocks in the AI and chip sectors. All three benchmark indices in New York lost over 2% each.

The Nikkei 225 tanked 5.1% to a seven-month low, while the broader Topix benchmark fell 3.9%. The KOSPI also tumbled 5.2%, while Taiwan's TAIEX slumped 6.2%.

Elsewhere, the Hang Seng in Hong Kong fell 1.9% while the Shanghai Composite dropped 1.2% and Singapore's STI slipped 2.0%.

“Asian markets rounded off a week from hell as investors dumped tech stocks across the board,” said Russ Mould, investment director at AJ Bell.

“Investors are catching up with the news earlier this week that Japanese data centre operator Datasection slashed its annual revenue forecast by 89% due to the cancellation of a major AI infrastructure order. Investors are naturally asking if this is the first domino falling, with the AI build-out story ripe for a potential slowdown."

SoftBank slumped over 14% in Tokyo, with Nikkei-listed Advantest, Kioxia, Tokyo Electron and Fujikura not too far behind.

In South Korea, tech giants Samsung Electronics, SK Hynix and Samsung Electro-Mechanics all finished with big losses, along with blue chip auto group Hyundai Motor.

Internet technology group NetEase was a heavy faller in Hong Kong after quarterly earnings disappointed, with Q3 revenues down 2% year-on-year to RMB27.9bn. Sector peer Kuaishou Technology also sank after posting a bigger-than-expected loss for the third quarter.

“The slightest bit of bad news is sending shivers down the spines of tech investors as some fear the good times could be over," Mould said.

"The tech trade has always been about accessing fast growth stories, and it’s been a winning ticket to wealth creation for quite some time. Cracks are now appearing in the narrative, and investors seem to be locking in some of their profits."

In economic news, Japanese inflation accelerated to an 11-month high of 2.3% in October from 2.1% in September, while Taiwanese exports surged 79% over last year to a record $124bn in October.

data.title: The Seven Charts That Explain the New Normal for Oil Prices — WSJ
data.description:
By Rebecca Feng

In the run-up to the U.S. midterm elections, Brent oil futures approached their highest level since the start of the war. Prices have since come down but are still well above $73 a barrel, the level the day before the war.

Now oil traders and analysts are coming to a consensus: The Strait of Hormuz might not return to what it was before the war, and consequently, oil prices of around $85 to $95 a barrel are poised to be the reality for the foreseeable future.

Stubbornly high crude prices are keeping prices elevated at the pump. As of Friday, regular gasoline averaged $3.69 a gallon in the U.S., according to AAA. That is down from a high of $4.56 in May, but a long way from $2.98 a gallon before the war.

These charts show the competing forces that are keeping oil prices from rising or falling too much:

Shipping attacks remain high...

One of the most important factors keeping oil prices from dropping further, analysts say, is the persistent attacks on oil tankers. In October alone, 35 ships were hit while transiting the Strait of Hormuz, threatening to cut off Middle Eastern oil from reaching global buyers, according to the International Maritime Organization. Tallies by maritime security firms point to a higher number. So far this month, about 20 attacks have occurred, according to the Royal Navy-affiliated U.K. Maritime Trade Operations and maritime security firms.

...sending the cost of transporting oil skyrocketing

Shipping crude on a very large carrier from the Middle East Gulf to Asia now costs $31.30 a barrel, less than in recent weeks but still about five times prewar levels, according to Argus Media, a price reporting agency.

Meanwhile, with more ships tied up conducting the high-risk, high-reward activity known as shuttle runs in the Strait of Hormuz, global freight costs on other popular routes have soared too.

Analysts generally agree that at least some of the high cost of delivering oil is passed on to the ultimate buyers.

The shuttle runs have boosted exports...

Persian Gulf oil exports, including shipments through Hormuz and alternative routes across the region, have recovered to around 17.1 million barrels a day in the week through Nov. 18, about 73% of prewar levels of 23.3 million, according to ship tracker Kpler. The output has at times briefly touched or slightly exceeded prewar levels.

The high volume of oil flowing through the Strait of Hormuz is a key reason why prices have started to stabilize, said Hamad Hussain, senior economist at Capital Economics. "However, this equilibrium is extremely fragile," he said, adding that attacks on oil tankers and energy infrastructure could trigger sharp drops in oil flows and flip the market from a surplus into a deficit.

...but global inventory is still sapped

Global observed oil inventories — including those held in on-land tanks, on-water vessels as well as governments' strategic petroleum reserves — rebounded slightly in October. However, even after the rebound, there is still a cumulative 462 million barrels of inventory drawdown since the start of the war, according to the International Energy Agency, a Paris-based energy watchdog. That is roughly four days of the world's oil consumption.

Refilling those stockpiles will keep a floor under prices.

"We've unwound the first layer of geopolitical risk premium that contains inflammatory rhetoric and the threat of attacks, and are now in this phase of talk of mediation with a dim prospect of a deal," said Naveen Das, senior crude analyst at ship-tracking data provider Kpler. With no breakthrough in diplomatic talks but no military escalation either, oil prices are now in a holding pattern, he said.

Gulf oil producers are ramping up production...

As shipments rise, countries including Iraq and Saudi Arabia are pumping out crude. That has tipped the global oil market into a small surplus in the last quarter of this year and a bigger surplus next year, according to the IEA.

However, analysts emphasized that a surplus is useless unless oil can actually get to global markets. "The predicted surplus is contingent on volumes leaving the Middle East without a U.S. naval presence in the region," said Kpler's Das.

...but China is back

The impact of the additional oil supply is in part being offset by more demand from China.

Chinese refiners in recent weeks have returned to the global market to buy crude. But analysts cautioned that China is sensitive to price, and the current levels are too high for the country to start aggressively stockpiling again.

Write to Rebecca Feng at rebecca.feng@wsj.com

data.title: Two Chinese copper smelters blend concentrate overseas to boost supply, sources say
data.description:
Key points:
  • China Minmetals starts overseas blending on trial basis in third quarter, sources say
  • China Copper has engaged in overseas blending for around one year, sources say
  • CRU pegs global copper concentrate deficit at 289,000 metric tons this year

Two large Chinese smelters have begun blending copper concentrate at a Malaysian port in a bid to boost supply amid a worsening feedstock shortage, four people with knowledge of the matter told Reuters.

China is by far the world's largest copper ore processor. But its rules strictly limit the allowable levels of toxins such as arsenic, meaning that only about one-fifth of concentrate produced outside the country meets import standards.

Blending higher-standard concentrate grades with those containing more toxins can allow more concentrate volumes to meet Chinese regulations. China, however, limits the number of different concentrates that can be blended domestically.

So, in order to broaden the availability of supply that can be processed in China, integrated producer China Minmetals Nonferrous Metals and smelter China Copper have been blending complex copper concentrate containing high impurities in Port Klang, Malaysia, the people said.

China Copper has engaged in overseas blending for around a year, while China Minmetals started doing so on a trial basis in the third quarter of this year, two of the people said.

It was not immediately clear how much copper concentrate the two smelters have blended in the Malaysian port.

China Minmetals and China Copper did not immediately respond to requests for comment.

The blending of complex copper concentrates has been allowed in bonded zones at domestic ports since 2020 and currently takes place at ports including Dalian, Yantai and Fangcheng.

However, blending overseas provides flexibility to mix several different types of concentrate while more stringent requirements apply for blending domestically, said one of the people.

International trading houses have long blended concentrates at ports outside China to meet its import standards. The overseas blending by the two Chinese smelters, however, has not been previously reported.

All the people requested anonymity as the information is not public.

The copper concentrate shortage worsened this year as smelting capacity expanded and disruptions reduced mined supply, driving unexpectedly high production cuts in China in the fourth quarter.

Consultancy CRU pegged the global copper concentrate deficit at 289,000 metric tons this year, versus 2,000 tons in 2025. Analysts expect mined copper supply to improve in 2027, but not enough to fill the gap.

Global copper concentrate supply is projected to grow by 4% in 2027 following a 0.4% rise this year, according to CRU.

data.title: Court Dismisses Challenge To Security Exemption For Oil Drilling In Gulf Of America
data.description:
WASHINGTON (dpa-AFX) - The U.S. District Court for the District of Columbia has dismissed a lawsuit challenging the first national security exemption ever issued pursuant to the Endangered Species Act.

The exemption terminated litigation threatening oil and gas exploration in the Gulf of America - a critical source of domestic production. The court held that it lacked jurisdiction because Congress directed all challenges to the Committee's exemption decisions to the federal courts of appeals, not the district courts.

'Energy security is national security, and Endangered Species Committee's exemption is ensuring continued domestic production of 15 percent of the nation's oil,' said Principal Deputy Assistant Attorney General Adam Gustafson of the Justice Department's Energy and Natural Resources Division, or ENRD.

'The district court agreed with us that legal challenges to such an exemption can only be heard in the courts of appeals. ENRD will continue to advance President Donald Trump's commitment to unleash American energy.'

On March 31, the Endangered Species Committee voted unanimously to grant an exemption for Gulf of America oil and gas activities, acting on the Secretary of War's finding that the exemption was necessary for reasons of national security. It was the first exemption the Committee has granted on national security grounds.

Several environmental groups then sued the decision in district courts. According to the motion to dismiss, Congress assigned judicial review of the Committee's exemption decisions to the appellate courts. The district court agreed in this case, concluding that Congress created only one type of exemption and 'funneled challenges to those exemptions to the courts of appeals.' It dismissed the entire case for lack of jurisdiction, including the plaintiff's related claims challenging the Secretary of War's national security finding and its claims under the National Environmental Policy Act.

The ruling follows decisions earlier this year by federal courts in the District of Columbia, Maryland, and Louisiana that gave effect to the Committee's exemption. Department of Justice said that with the federal court's ruling, the exemption for Gulf of America oil and gas exploration activities remains in place.

data.title: Accor's top investor calls for urgent leadership change
data.description:
Accor's top shareholder, Parvus Asset Management Jersey, called for urgent change in the hotel operator's leadership late on Thursday, citing prolonged underperformance and what the activist investor described as inconsistent strategic decisions.

"We have exhausted our efforts to engage privately. In our view, inconsistent messaging, particularly from the highest levels of leadership, and repeated changes in strategic direction have broken confidence," Parvus said in a statement, adding it would use all shareholder rights at its disposal to hold Accor's management accountable.

  • The investor, whose funds hold close to 15% of Accor's shares, said the group had "materially underperformed" its peers over the long term under CEO Sébastien Bazin

  • Accor shares have delivered significantly lower returns during Bazin's tenure than rivals including IHG , Hilton and Marriott , Parvus said

  • It attributed the gap to Accor's "unfocused" strategy, inconsistent capital allocation and inadequate oversight

  • The investor also criticised Accor's handling of lifestyle hospitality venture Ennismore

  • "Accor faces its most consequential capital-allocation decisions in a decade, with significant strategic choices still to be made ... an outgoing leadership team should not be setting long-term strategy nor make any large capital-allocation decisions," Parvus said

  • Accor declined to comment on Parvus' demands

  • Accor's shares slid 1.8% in morning trade

data.title: SEBI to float paper on easing FPI constraints
data.description:
Foreign portfolio investors may find it easier to operate in Indian markets, with SEBI preparing a consultation paper to remove certain India-specific regulatory constraints that are not present in major global jurisdictions.

SEBI Chairman Tuhin Kanta Pandey said the proposal is part of the regulator’s effort to broaden the pool of overseas capital and bring India’s FPI framework closer to international practice. “Very soon, we will also release a consultation paper to further simplify FPI operations in India by suggesting removal of some of the other constraints that other countries don’t have, but we do have,” he said at the CII Financing Summit.

The regulator has already digitised several parts of the FPI registration process. It now accepts digitally signed powers of attorney and has enabled net settlement to lower funding costs, while working to reduce onboarding time to as little as five business days.

A joint working group of SEBI and the Reserve Bank of India is expected to begin work immediately on a common application form and further simplification of registration procedures.

“Onboarding is already happening through simplified processes. But we see that there is further scope to simplify it, and we are working towards that,” Pandey said.

In a separate easing of access, eligible non-resident Indians will no longer need to travel to India for KYC. They can complete the process through video-based verification, for which detailed guidelines have already been issued.

Pre-IPO

Pandey also said SEBI is refining a proposed pre-IPO framework, but has yet to settle the stage at which unlisted companies would become eligible or the safeguards that would govern investor participation.

“We are working on that. But the pre-IPO stage, where and how it will happen, and from which stage it will start, is being worked out in detail. You will get to know about it soon,” he said.

Bonds

On corporate bonds, SEBI is finalising a market-making framework intended to improve trading in the secondary market. Pandey said the design is still being worked out.

“Bond trading is happening in the secondary market and it is quite big now. But we need to increase secondary trading even more,” he said.

Tax

Pandey declined to comment on STT and LTCG proposals, saying these are matters for the government. He also said issues relating to GST in physically settled commodity derivatives have been raised with the concerned ministries and are before the GST Secretary.

“Scale will enable growth, stability will sustain it, trust will strengthen both,” he said.

data.title: Strand Life Sciences to take its multi-cancer blood test to more hospitals, looks to bring down cost: CEO
data.description:
Armed with test results from a four-year study, across local 43 hospitals, Strand Life Sciences is looking to make its multi-cancer early detection test, CancerSpot, available at more hospitals, even as it looks to bring down the cost on these DNA-based tests to the ₹10,000 range, said Chief Executive Officer Dr Ramesh Hariharan.

The non-invasive blood test helps detect cancer from the DNA of tumour cells circulating in the blood, and the study involving this early-detection test has been published in the Proceedings of the (US) National Academy of Sciences (PNAS).

This is a first of its kind study from India, said Hariharan, even as similar studies have been published in the United States and China. “The study used CancerSpot test on about 1,500 samples and showed that you can detect cancer with very low false positive rate, about 1.4 percent and with reasonable sensitivity so 70 per cent of cancers can be detected,” Hariharan told businessline.

Pointing to a novel finding, he said, “in cancer patients, the amount of DNA arising from immune cells also rises substantially, which would be expected to dilute the tumor contribution and thereby hamper cancer detection. This study shows the opposite.” The tumor and immune cell contributions in the circulating DNA appear to rise “in synchrony,” in cancer patients, the study noted.

CancerSpot combines DNA sequencing with AI to identify methylation patterns, or chemical modifications of the DNA, that distinguish cancer cells from normal cells, the company said. The DNA carries a signature pattern or address of where it was coming from - the heart, lungs, kidney, he said. Responding to whether it would be beneficial in early detection, he said, “clinical utility depends on walking a tightrope: maximising sensitivity to catch disease early while minimizing false-positives that lead to unnecessary invasive procedures and patient harm. Achieving that balance requires deep scientific insight and rigorous validation.”

Lower price

Strand Life Sciences, a subsidiary of Reliance Industries Limited, looks to take the test now to more hospitals, and hopes to bring down its cost to the ₹10,000 range, from the present ₹33,000, in a couple of years, he said. The test helps detect about 14 cancers, including lung cancer in non-smokers, stomach cancer, gallbladder cancer, pancreatic cancer, liver cancer, ovarian cancer and esophageal cancer – though brain cancer is a challenge, he indicated.

The liquid biopsy segment has companies like Guardant Health Inc, that has a US Food and Drug Administration-approved liquid biopsy panel; and Grail Inc that has received a favourable recommendation from the USFDA’s advisory committee. “The companies from the US will sell in India,” said, adding Guardant has already started, and Grail would come as well. “Chances are they’re going to be priced much higher. And at the moment at least, our data looks superior to Guardant and in some aspects superior to Grail,” he added. In India, Datar Genetics and Tzar Labs are said to have products in this segment.

While Strand’s operates in the business-to-business space in the US, he said, “the rest of the world, India, Asia, Middle East, Africa… is going to be our arena for this test.”

AZ tie-up

In a separate development, Strand LS had recently formalised a collaboration with AstraZeneca India, to explore healthcare opportunities. Both companies are investing in taking Strand’s cancer treatment selection tests to different State governments, he said, adding that it was already on in Andhra Pradesh. This could expand from treatment screening to screening, possibly at a later date, he added.

data.title: Ed Yardeni Says Anthropic Earnings Will Offer Clearer Picture Of AI Adoption, Sees Market Selloff As Buying Opportunity
data.description:
Key points:
  • Yardeni’s 7,900 S&P 500 target is based on projected 2027 EPS of $425 and a forward P/E of 18.6.
  • He suspects “some irrational exuberance” in analysts’ forecasts, with the consensus 2028 EPS at $496 versus Yardeni Research’s $450.
  • “We continue to view the recent selloff as a buying opportunity," Yardeni wrote.

Yardeni Research President Ed Yardeni said that Anthropic's future earnings reports will provide a clearer picture of artificial intelligence (AI) adoption across the economy, helping assess whether demand for computing power is strong enough to sustain the ongoing AI infrastructure buildout.

In his Quicktakes note, Yardeni also said financial, political, and physical constraints could slow the AI buildout but are unlikely to halt it as long as demand for compute continues to grow.

Yardeni expects panic selling to abate soon, noting that investors have pushed the S&P 500's forward price-to-earnings ratio down to 17.6, below its level during last year's Liberation Day selloff. "We continue to view the recent selloff as a buying opportunity," he wrote.

Anthropic Listing Amid Tech Selloff

Anthropic (ANT) raised $81.3 billion in its initial public offering (IPO), pricing shares at $83 apiece. The stock opened at $111.50 on Thursday, reached an intraday high of $115.10 and eventually closed at $97.17, up 17% from its IPO price.

The broader market reversed an early rally, with the S&P 500 and Nasdaq-100 index falling over 2%. Yardeni noted that AMD stock plunged nearly 8% following a short-seller report raising concerns about its ties to Chinese entities.

“Coming on the back of the Nvidia (NVDA) controversy and tighter US export controls, the report provided another reminder of the political speed bumps facing the AI trade,” Yardeni wrote.

Yardeni Maintains 7,900 S&P 500 Target

The latest market selloff followed several weeks of weakness in technology and AI-related stocks. Over the last month, the Nasdaq-100 has tumbled over 10%. Semiconductor stocks suffered steeper losses over the same period.

The iShares Semiconductor ETF (SOXX) declined over 17%, while the VanEck Semiconductor ETF (SMH) fell more than 18%. The Roundhill Memory ETF (DRAM), which provides exposure to memory-related companies, has also slipped more than 19%.

Despite the market weakness, Yardeni maintained his S&P 500 target of 7,900, based on projected 2027 earnings per share (EPS) of $425 and a forward price-to-earnings multiple of 18.6.

He noted that industry analysts continued raising earnings estimates, with the consensus 2028 EPS forecast reaching $496, compared with Yardeni Research's $450 EPS projection.

The Yardeni Research President highlighted analysts' optimistic forecasts. “We suspect some irrational exuberance, as these forecasts fail to account for the AI buildout's speed bumps,” he said.

data.title: Indonesia revokes forestry permit of pulp and paper unit of RGE, task force says
data.description:
Indonesia's forestry task force said on Friday it has revoked the forest usage permit of PT Riau Andalan Pulp and Paper, a unit of the Royal Golden Eagle Group, covering 338,536 hectares (836,541 acres), according to a statement.

  • The forestry permit was revoked by the Forestry Ministry due to a number of violations, including recurring forest fires within the concession, the task force said

  • The task force also found palm oil plantations and mining activities in the area, it said

  • Business activities in the concession shall cease immediately, but the company is still subject to environmental restoration obligations, the task force said

  • RAPP said in a statement it "respect the government's authority and will continue to engage constructively with the relevant authorities"

  • The company is awaiting formal notification and further clarification from the government, and will respond through the appropriate processes

  • Royal Golden Eagle Group is a resource-based conglomerate controlled by billionaire Sukanto Tanoto, one of Indonesia's richest people

  • Indonesia formed the forestry task force, consisting of prosecutors, the military and forestry officials, last year to resolve conflicting forestry permits

  • The task force has as of October seized more than 6 million hectares from plantation and mining companies accused of violating regulations

  • Indonesia is battling its most intense forest fire in 11 years this year amid prolonged dry weather caused by the El Niño weather phenomenon

  • Experts have said fire risks in Indonesia have been made worse by extensive land clearances and the drainage of peatland to make way for pulp and palm oil concessions

data.title: US yields fall as AI trade worries spur safe-haven bid
data.description:
By Sophie Kiderlin

US Treasury yields dropped on Friday as jitters about the AI trade weighed on global equities and led investors to seek out safe-haven assets.

Anthropic's market debut on Thursday saw shares in the world's first publicly traded frontier AI company jump, but failed to bring back confidence in the broader AI trade. Concerns about the sector's rising spending and debt load, Jensen Huang's departure from Nvidia, and worries about tougher scrutiny and a deceleration of data-centre expansion after the Democrats' midterm sweep have all weighed on investor sentiment in recent weeks.

MSCI's world index of stocks fell for a seventh straight session EURONEXT:IACWI, and futures for the tech-heavy Nasdaq 100 were last down by over 1%.

The yield on the 10-year Treasury note was last down 5.8 basis points to 4.9958%, back below the 5% mark. Across the week so far, the yield was down almost 16 bps, on track for its biggest weekly fall since mid-2025.

Bond prices rise as yields fall.

Investors were also weighing the outlook for interest rates from the Federal Reserve, and were paying close attention to any comments from policymakers about the possible rate path ahead. Federal Reserve Bank of Philadelphia President Anna Paulson said on Thursday the Fed will need to raise interest rates again because inflation is too high.

Fed funds futures traders were last pricing in an almost 100% chance of a 25-basis-point hike at the US central bank's December 8-9 meeting, according to the CME Group's FedWatch Tool. A larger, 50-basis-point increase has also been brought into the mix, although money market expectations for such a hike have been pared back.

The 2-year yield (US2YT=RR) was last down around 6 bps to 4.7194% on the day. It was last down over 15 basis points this week so far, also on track for its steepest weekly drop since mid-2025.

data.title: ECB's Santos Pereira says energy-driven inflation pressures are a concern
data.description:
Energy-driven inflation pressures are significant, with rising natural gas prices representing a particular concern for policymakers, though it is not yet clear whether they have spread to the wider euro zone economy, European Central Bank Governing Council member Alvaro Santos Pereira said on Friday.

"We are in a situation, in terms of inflation, with very significant pressures ... the big question is whether it spreads from energy to other parts of the economy, with second-round effects," Santos Pereira, who heads the Bank of Portugal, told a conference hosted by Portuguese business daily Jornal de Negocios.

He pointed to higher inflation in energy products such as oil, natural gas and refined products, citing uncertainty over the reopening of the Strait of Hormuz amid continuing tanker disruptions there.

Santos Pereira said the rise in natural gas prices "is something that concerns us" because of low storage levels in some northern European countries, adding: "If we have a cold winter we could have, in some countries, some storage disruptions and pressure on electricity prices."

Euro zone inflation climbed to a three-year high of 4.0% in October, twice the ECB's 2% medium-term target, driven by surging energy and food prices. Energy inflation alone clocked 20.8%.

data.title: DAX Tumbles 1.64% Amid AI Concerns; Producer Prices Hit 3-Year Peak
data.description:
BRUSSELS (dpa-AFX) - Germany's equity benchmark DAX tumbled on Friday, as concerns about sustainability of AI trade returned to haunt the tech sector despite Anthropic's successful IPO offering and the stock's subsequent sterling debut on Wall Street yesterday.

After a strong debut on Thursday, Anthropic shares shed ground in after-hours trading as the euphoria over its record IPO subsided.

Concerns about inflation and possibile interest rate hike by the Federal Reserve and a few other central banks in the coming months weighed as well on sentiment.

The DAX, extending its decline to a sixth straight session, was down 417.74 points or 1.64% at 25,081.17 a little over half an hour before noon. The index dropped to a low of 24,918.94 earlier in the session.

Scout24, Infineon Technologies and Siemens Energy lost 6%, 5.5% and 5.4%, respectively. Hochtief drifted lower by 4.3%, while Siemens, Deutsche Bank and RWE shed 3.1%-3.7%.

Deutsche Post, Commerzbank, Continental, MTU Aero Engines, Rheinmetall, Deutsche Boerse, SAP, BASF, Allianz, Daimler Truck Holding, Merck, Heidelberg Materials, Adidas, Gea Group, Bayer, Brenntag and Zalando lost 1%-3%.

Fresenius Medical Care climbed about 2.5%. Vonovia moved up 1.8%, while Hannover RE, Deutsche Telekom and Beiersdorf gained 0.8%-1.1%. BMW and Munich RE posted modest gains.

Data released by Destatis showed Germany's producer prices increased at the fastest pace in more than three years in October on rising energy and intermediate goods prices.

Producer prices grew 8.1% year-on-year in October, marking the strongest growth since February 2023. Economists had forecast prices to climb 7.2% after posting an annual growth of 6.7% in September.

On a monthly basis, producer prices gained 1.4% compared to economists' forecast of 0.9%.

The annual increase in producer prices was primarily due to the 18.7% surge in energy prices. The prices of intermediate goods also increased substantially, up by 6.8%.

data.title: Naphtha market weakens; KPC offers December gasoline
data.description:
Asia's naphtha prices declined on Friday in tandem with crude oil and as window activity remained muted amid lacklustre demand, traders and analysts said.

The price for first-half January naphtha fell by about $6 to $818.50 per metric ton. The price structure remained in wide backwardation of $16.50 a ton.

In spot purchases, South Korean and Japanese buyers surfaced in the market this week, with premiums ranging from $20 to $30 per ton to Japan quotes for first-half January cargoes, market participants said.

In the gasoline market, Kuwait Petroleum Corp offered 34,000-35,000 metric tons of 93-octane non-oxygenated gasoline in a tender on a free-on-board (FOB) basis from its Mina Al-Ahmadi port, a document reviewed by Reuters showed.

The cargo is scheduled to load between December 9 and December 10, according to the tender, which closed on Wednesday.

The gasoline crack extended losses and lingered near three-year lows due to ample supplies from China and the Middle East, traders said.

NEWS

- More Russian regions are introducing restrictions on retail sales of gasoline and diesel following a renewed spate of Ukrainian attacks on oil refineries, according to local media and authorities.

- Oil prices edged down on Friday and were set for a weekly decline on strong exports from the Middle East despite Houthi attacks on Saudi Arabia's capital Riyadh and reports of tanker disruptions in the Strait of Hormuz.

data.title: TSX futures slip as lower oil, gold prices weigh; retail sales data eyed
data.description:
Futures tracking Canada's blue-chip stocks fell on Friday as lower oil and gold prices weighed on sentiment, while investors awaited domestic retail sales data due later in the day.

December futures on the S&P/TSX 60 index (SXFcv1) were down 0.36% at 05:32 a.m. ET (1032 GMT).

  • Brent crude shed about 2%, heading for a third straight weekly decline on strong exports from the Middle East despite Houthi attacks on Saudi Arabia's capital Riyadh and reports of tanker disruptions in the Strait of Hormuz

  • Gold prices, meanwhile, were headed for their worst week in eight months, as expectations of a Federal Reserve interest-rate hike in December supported the dollar

  • The spotlight is also on domestic retail sales data, due at 08:30 ET, which will be closely watched for signals on the health of Canadian consumers

  • Separately, Canada is still seeking a temporary deal to ease US tariffs on its goods, though Washington has shown little willingness to budge, Trade Minister Dominic LeBlanc told an advisory committee on Thursday, sources said

  • US futures fell and stock markets across the globe tumbled after Anthropic's IPO failed to restore investors' faith in the AI sector

  • On Thursday, Canada's main stock index fell for a sixth straight day as a selloff in gold extended, with metal mining and technology shares pacing broad-based declines

  • In company news, Bausch + Lomb said its experimental eye-drop treatment failed to significantly reduce pain during the first 24 hours after laser eye surgery in a mid-stage study
